body:
Rereview: TEST-SR-03 now expressly admits justified diagnostic contribution that materially helps identify the protected failure, requires its explanation, and rejects different names or repeated assertions alone as evidence of that value. Independently read the revised requirement with TEST-SR-01/04/05/07/08 and the glossary, representative examples, consumer inventory and acceptance table. A focused lower-level case may aid failure localization even where an integrated test detects the same defect; it still needs a governing obligation, meaningful oracle and valid observation boundary. The clarification therefore reconciles case selection with the already-selected diagnostic criterion without weakening removal protection or permitting arbitrary case proliferation. Workflow and approved proposal remain unchanged; all six complete-package conclusions below were reassessed and remain justified. Fresh structural evidence binds the revised package. No prior finding requires disposition and no new material concern arose.

Scope: isolated independent Design Review of the exact two-member package test (docs/design/test/test.md) and workflow (docs/design/workflow/workflow.md). Upstream basis is the current approved proposal-review for Design-Derived Test Model and its unchanged exact proposal. Review and Closeout, Record Format and CLI are governing dependencies, not silently added package members. Unified model Design combines architecture/requirements/decisions under the authorized model-document convention; no separate ADR is applicable.

Six package criteria:
1. Behavior and architecture: pass. TEST-SR-01–13 have an achievable policy architecture through existing authoring, planning, implementation and assessment activities. Group-level many-to-many traceability preserves an independent oracle and plausible violation without a ledger or test-function bureaucracy. Runtime examples and quality acceptance explain actual outcomes; no new runner, gate or CLI quality selector is needed.
2. Constraints: pass. Product/component Design retains intended behavior and compatibility retirement. Test owns purpose, derivation, protective value and maintenance criteria; specialists apply them to concrete subjects under RC authority/applicability/closeout policy. Record Format narrative/evidence fields are sufficient for the selected rationale, with no speculative schema change. Explicit adoption and historical-contract boundaries prevent global reinterpretation or deletion authorization.
3. Proposal preservation: pass. Both design-derived creation and actual bounded existing-suite audit/cleanup remain mandatory downstream scope. Delivery must name suites, candidate scope, completion outcomes and protection evidence; no deletion quota is imposed, and a justified retain/uncertain outcome cannot be disguised as an unperformed audit. The latest user clarification is explicit in Test Context and Scope, TEST-SR-11, Quality criteria versus assessment, Workflow WF-SR-17 and WF-DEC-06.
4. Boundaries: pass. All eight dimensions have requirement-linked outcomes. The package separates current output from required output, mocks/helpers from claimed public behavior, case count from distinct contribution, and passing execution from sufficient/current evidence. Removal/replacement requires demonstrated retained protection or authorized retirement. Legacy unlabeled reproduction is preserved while its behavior authority is investigated. Flaky sole protection cannot disappear for green output; quarantine requires authorized limits, follow-up and alternative protection or accepted residual risk. Randomized tests keep a justified property/domain and enough counterexample/environment information for investigation. Discovery/selector loss is a proof gap, not successful simplification.
5. Decisions and dependencies: pass. Embedded TEST-DEC-01–05 and WF-DEC-06 agree with responsibilities and preserve existing RC requirements. WF-SR-17 routes behavioral, allocation and concrete-test defects to their owning activities without making Test an approval principal. Existing final independent Code Review and distinct Verify remain unwaived. No new external-action or rollback permission is inferred.
6. Delivery sufficiency/coherence: pass. The consumer inventory assigns criterion families to retained owners and Test requirements, preserves specialist and historical methods, and requires exact transitive file/disposition expansion before implementation. Newly discovered policy conflicts return to Design rather than being decided by consumer edits. Acceptance requires requirement/scenario/combined-hazard allocation, focused real-result evidence and portable selectively loaded resources. Exact case inventory, filenames, fixtures, commands and package generation remain legitimate Delivery/implementation choices, not missing Design decisions.

Acceptance review specifically considered consolidation plus lost public-path protection; a flaky sole regression with missing behavior authority; and faster validation caused by discovery omission. TEST-SR-02/04/07–11 define preservation, owned investigation/correction and bounded claims for those combinations; RC selects the overall judgment. Vacuous assertions, production-derived expected results, unchecked snapshots, unsupported-version retirement and randomized external-state failures are covered. Evidence reuse remains RC-SR-15-owned and a new review does not itself force all commands to rerun. Restoration of removed tests is distinguished from policy rollback and cannot restore stale evidence automatically.

Evidence and limitations: read both package members in full, the complete current proposal and its approved independent review, relevant RC/Workflow/Record Format/CLI boundaries, and representative canonical plan/boundary/code-review/bugfix consumer methods. All relied-on subjects were mechanically inspected before the targeted write. design-structure records actual model validation, readability and whitespace checks; it is structural author evidence rather than this semantic judgment. The document's explicit-recording-v1 marker versions model structure, while the initiative's rigorloop-records-v2 selects record storage; no conflict exists. The model format expressly replaces the historical four-table feature serialization while retaining boundary reasoning.

I independently confirmed the two unresolved historical Workflow proposal links were already present at HEAD and their files are absent. They occur in prior-amendment history and are not the current Test proposal, its approval, a selected requirement owner, or an acceptance dependency. The current amendment explicitly scopes old inventories/history; therefore this baseline navigation debt does not remove required authority or prevent assessing this package. No historical approval is retargeted or missing proposal reconstructed.

Optional advisory navigation improvement: Workflow's model-layout illustration could include test/test.md beside its earlier four models. Current model inventory, explicit Test link, generic equal-directory/file rule and exact registered package already resolve the path, so the omission does not create an unmet behavior or ownership condition and is not a required finding.

No existing suite has been audited here, no case found safe to delete, and no implementation/protection-preservation/Verify success is claimed. Return at the isolated review boundary; planning, consumer edits, test cleanup and routing remain separately authorized activities.
independence_basis: Separate delegated reviewer /root/independent_proposal_review did not author or edit either model, its proposal or corrections. codex-author authored the package using user direction. This reviewer independently read both complete members, upstream approval and relevant dependencies, assessed coherence and writes only its review evidence. Prior participation in this initiative was independent Proposal Review, not engineering authorship.
